why: A cron sweep (tick hye) selects work with nobody asking, from tick records
Go owns. cloud/factory/src/sweeps.ts is therefore a THIRD reader of
internal/tick.Tick's on-disk shape, and it reads more of it than
tick-membership.ts does: status, priority, type, labels, blocked_by,
created_at, awaiting/manual and requires.
It matters which way this reader fails. A field renamed in Go alone would
not break a sweep loudly — the TypeScript parser is deliberately tolerant,
so a missing `priority` reads as 'lowest possible' and a missing `status`
reads as 'not closed'. The sweep would keep running every weekday morning,
selecting from keys that are no longer there, with both suites green. This
fixture is what makes that a red test instead.
Checked from internal/tick/sweep_selection_parity_test.go and from
cloud/factory/test/sweep-contract.test.ts.
Go's Tick.IsAwaitingHuman is `Awaiting != nil || Manual` — two spellings of
the same state, the second a legacy flag. A sweep must honour BOTH, because
the whole point of the predicate here is that time-based ignition never
picks up work a person is holding.
Both are omitempty in Go, so the common case is that neither key is present.
The design doc's rule for a sweep is 'priority, then age, then ID' —
docs/design/cloud-factory.md, UC7 step 3. That is deliberately NOT the same
comparator as internal/wave.Compute's, which sorts a wave by priority then
ID with no age term: a wave orders ticks that are all being run anyway,
while a sweep CHOOSES which few of a backlog run at all, and a chooser with
no age term starves the oldest tick forever.
The difference is recorded here so it reads as a decision rather than as
drift. If wave.Compute ever grows an age term, the two become the same rule
and this note is what says they were compared.
order.rule: priority asc, created_at asc, id asc

why: Where a sweep policy is declared, and in which format. The design doc
writes it as a markdown bullet in .tick/config.md; it is implemented
against .tick/runners.toml for the reason tick 0vb settled for
[signals.sources.*] — a program-parsed surface that must fail closed on a
typo needs a schema, and config.md's machine-parsed sections were
deprecated by epic 48d.
Listed here rather than only in prose because it is the one part of the
sweep an operator writes by hand.
